subject: surgery
title: Deep Anorectal Infections, Prolapse, and Anal Malignancy

steps.tx: A deep purulent infection expanding within the fat-filled space between the obturator internus and anal canal is an **ischiorectal abscess**. The abundant, poorly vascularized adipose tissue of the ischioanal fossa permits rapid, unchecked bacterial multiplication. Patients present with high swinging pyrexia, chills, tachycardia, and deep-seated, throbbing pelvic pain, frequently without early visible cutaneous redness at the perineal surface.
steps.say: An ischiorectal abscess expands rapidly in the deep fatty ischioanal fossa, presenting with high fever and throbbing buttock pain.

vis.alt: Surgical technique of wide incision and drainage of an abscess using the Hilton method with loculation breakdown.
vis.caption: Incision and drainage: wide deroofing and loculation breakdown required for deep ischiorectal abscesses. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Tracking of purulent infection from one ischioanal fossa across the posterior midline produces a **horseshoe abscess communication**. Infection travels through the deep postanal space of Courtney located posterior to the anal canal and deep to the anococcygeal ligament. Successful surgical eradication requires deroofing the primary crypt infection in the posterior midline combined with wide bilateral counter-drainage incisions over each ischiorectal fossa.
steps.say: A horseshoe abscess spreads across the deep postanal space of Courtney, necessitating bilateral counter-drainage incisions.

nodes.label: Spread into Deep Postanal Space of Courtney
Bilateral Extension into Both Ischioanal Fossae

steps.tx: Circumferential full-thickness intussusception and protrusion of all layers of the rectal wall through the anus is **rectal prolapse**. Known clinically as procidentia, it presents as a bulky, reddish cylindrical mass displaying concentric circular mucosal folds, distinguishing it from the radial folds seen in prolapsed haemorrhoids. It predominantly afflicts elderly multiparous females with pelvic floor attenuation, profound sphincter laxity, and deep pouch of Douglas.
steps.say: Complete rectal prolapse shows concentric mucosal rings, distinguishing full-thickness procidentia from prolapsed internal haemorrhoids.

left.title: Complete Rectal Prolapse (Procidentia)
points: Full-thickness extrusion of all rectal wall layers
Characterized by concentric circular mucosal folds
Associated with severe fecal incontinence and laxity
Requires abdominal or perineal surgical repair

right.title: Mucosal Prolapse / Prolapsed Haemorrhoids
points: Only mucosal and submucosal layers protrude
Anal sphincter tone remains normal or increased
Treated by rubber band ligation or haemorrhoidectomy

steps.tx: The definitive gold standard surgical correction of complete rectal prolapse in medically fit patients is **rectopexy procedures**. Utilizing a laparoscopic approach, the surgeon mobilizes the rectum down to the pelvic floor, elevates the mobilized organ out of the pelvis, and secures it to the presacral fascia and sacral promontory with permanent sutures or synthetic prosthetic mesh, restoring normal pelvic anatomy and continence.
steps.say: Laparoscopic rectopexy elevates and anchors the prolapsed rectum to the sacral promontory, restoring continence and anatomical alignment.

rows: Fit patients with prolapse and rectocele
Mesh on anterior rectum, avoids posterior nerves

steps.tx: For elderly, frail, or debilitated individuals who cannot safely tolerate abdominal laparotomy or general anaesthesia, surgeons perform **perineal prolapse repair**. The Delorme procedure strips the redundant rectal mucosa and plicates the denuded rectal muscularis like an accordion. Alternatively, the Altemeier operation performs a perineal rectosigmoidectomy, excising the redundant prolapsed bowel transanally and fashioning a primary coloanal anastomosis with minimal physiological stress.
steps.say: Perineal repairs like the Delorme or Altemeier operations correct rectal prolapse transanally in frail, high-risk patients.

nodes.label: Elderly Patient with Medical Comorbidities & Prolapse
Perineal Resection or Mucosal Stripping & Plication

steps.tx: A squamous cell malignancy arising in the mucosal lining of the anal canal or anal margin is **anal carcinoma**. Strongly linked to persistent infection with high-risk oncogenic human papillomavirus serotypes sixteen and eighteen, this malignancy is increasingly encountered in immunocompromised patients, particularly those living with HIV. Typical clinical presentations include anal bleeding, pain, tenesmus, and a palpable indurated ulcerated mass with rolled everted edges.
steps.say: Anal carcinoma is a squamous cell malignancy driven by high-risk human papillomavirus, presenting with bleeding and indurated ulceration.

vis.alt: Perianal inspection diagram illustrating examination of indurated anal verge ulceration and clock-face orientation.
vis.caption: Anal cancer: ulcerated anal mass with bleeding and enlarged inguinal lymph nodes. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: The established standard primary organ-preserving curative treatment for squamous cell anal canal carcinoma is the **Nigro protocol**. Formulated in 1974, this definitive regimen combines pelvic external beam radiation therapy totaling 45 to 50 Gray with concurrent infusional 5-fluorouracil and mitomycin C. This primary chemoradiation achieves complete pathological tumor response in over eighty percent of patients, rendering permanent colostomy unnecessary in the vast majority.
steps.say: The Nigro chemoradiation protocol cures over eighty percent of squamous anal cancers while preserving anal sphincter function.

nodes.label: Histological Confirmation of Squamous Cell Carcinoma
Pelvic External Beam Radiotherapy (45 to 50 Gray)

steps.tx: Radical surgical excision of the anorectum is reserved strictly as a secondary measure known as **salvage abdominoperineal resection**. This radical operation is indicated solely for patients exhibiting persistent viable tumor at post-chemoradiation assessment at twelve to twenty-six weeks, or for those who develop biopsy-proven locoregional recurrence following an initial complete response to the Nigro protocol.
steps.say: Salvage abdominoperineal resection is reserved strictly for persistent or recurrent anal cancer following definitive chemoradiation.

left.title: Primary Nigro Chemoradiation
points: First-line treatment for all non-metastatic anal cancers
Preserves native anal sphincter and fecal continence
Combines pelvic radiotherapy with 5-FU and mitomycin C
Complete clinical response achieved in > 80% of cases

right.title: Salvage Abdominoperineal Resection
points: Reserved strictly for radiation failure or relapse
Total en bloc excision of rectum and anal sphincter
High rate of perineal wound healing complications

steps.tx: Distressing, intractable perianal itching arising from a diverse spectrum of local and systemic disorders is **pruritus ani**. Aetiological factors encompass fecal soiling from haemorrhoids or skin tags, pinworm Enterobius vermicularis infection in children, fungal candidiasis, contact dermatitis, and aggressive over-cleansing. Management centers on meticulous dry hygiene, wearing loose cotton underwear, eliminating perfumed soaps, and applying protective barrier creams.
steps.say: Pruritus ani is managed primarily by eliminating irritants, maintaining dry gentle hygiene, and treating underlying anorectal causes.

rows: Nocturnal perianal pruritus, positive tape test
Fiery red patch with satellite pustules
Treat primary condition, barrier zinc paste
